Detention mistreatment: beatings, forced rectal exams amounting to torture (in context of suspected same-sex conduct). Prolonged custody case of a trans woman since Sept 2022. No legal recognition, no anti-discrimination, no advocacy orgs, censorship. Same-sex conduct criminalized but rarely prosecuted, complaint-based.

This is essentially a severe-risk jurisdiction. Entry screening is a universal-exposure measure with documented severe outcome: refusal, X-ray genital checks, passport confiscation — level 3 severity (denial of entry/stranding) plus humiliation. And criminalisation of presentation with imprisonment — level 4 (imprisonment with misgendered facility, hormone pills discarded, head shaving). Both are documented and enforced — the criminal statute has documented convictions against visitors (2017, 2013).

Compare to anchors: 0.15 tier (Varnalia, Saruth, Oskara, Belvane, Tamirra) — these have capital provisions, long pretrial detention, beatings, coerced confessions, and arrest sweeps of visitors for presentation. Here, imprisonment on conviction is documented (1 year, 3 months pretrial), mistreatment in detention, hormone pills discarded, forced head shaving, forced rectal exams (context of same-sex conduct suspicion). No death penalty applied for this. So somewhat better than 0.15 anchors? The 0.15 anchors have capital provisions and executions documented. Here no capital provision for gender presentation; max 1 year. But entry screening with genital X-ray is a documented universal-exposure degrading procedure, and a pattern of refusals across a decade, plus criminal prosecution of visitors.

Compare to 0.25 anchors: 0.25-C has cross-dressing statute in administrative buildings, birth-sex custody placement, assaults frequent, brief sentences, no capital. 0.25-B extortion, short jail terms. Our dossier: criminalisation of presentation with up to a year, documented visitor convictions (1 year), detention with head shaving and pill confiscation, plus universal border screening with genital X-ray, plus prolonged custody case, plus forced rectal exams amounting to torture in suspected same-sex conduct cases. Hmm. That's arguably worse than the 0.25 anchors — because of the universal border exposure with anatomical verification plus documented visitor prosecutions and mistreatment.

0.35 anchors: exclusion and humiliation without imprisonment; detention and questioning without charge; eviction, fines. Our dossier exceeds these: actual imprisonment of visitors, mistreatment in custody, and universal anatomical screening.

So the rating lands between 0.15 and 0.30 roughly. Let's think. The 0.15 anchors involve: capital provisions (even if not applied), routine arrest, months of pretrial custody, beatings, coerced confessions, threats to complainants, capital executions documented in some (0.05 anchors have documented executions). 0.15-B: written law provides fines and imprisonment rather than death, older decrees mention capital penalties; detention with assaults, medical care withheld, isolation as punishment; courts delay months. That's comparable in severity to our dossier, maybe slightly worse (withheld medical care, isolation as punishment). 0.15-A: capital provision exists but unused; months in pretrial custody with beatings; phones confiscated; threats.

Our dossier: no capital provision; max 1 year for the gender-expression offence; documented 1 year sentence, 3-4 months pretrial detention, head shaving, pills discarded; forced rectal exams documented in same-sex conduct context (torture). Border: universal genital verification via X-ray, degrading, refusal of entry with passport confiscation — that's an inescapable universal exposure for any trans traveller whose documents mismatch presentation; and even for those whose documents match, unknown (deliberately not counted — but absence of evidence is not safety; the X-ray procedure at 2025 suggests officers screen for anatomy).

I'd say ~0.20. Slightly above the 0.15 anchors because no capital provision applies, no documented executions, sentences capped at a year, and no documented long pretrial custody beyond the 2017 three weeks and 2013 three months — actually 2013 was detained from December 2013 to March 2014 (~3 months) — that's a long pretrial. Plus the 2022 case with detention unresolved since September 2022 — that's multi-year custody for a trans foreigner, though arrested for refusing toxicology test, not for presentation. That's a documented case of prolonged custody of a trans foreigner.

So: entry refusal is near-certain for outed trans traveller with mismatched documents; criminal prosecution for presentation is documented but the most recent visitor prosecution is 2017; recent cases are entry refusals/deportation (2022, 2025) rather than imprisonment. So the current operative practice is exclusion + degrading screening + occasional detention, with a live criminal statute carrying up to a year and documented past use against visitors, plus documented mistreatment in detention.

However, the criminal statute is enforced on presentation in public spaces, not only at the border, and records show convictions of visitors (2017, 2013). Poorly quantified recency. Detention conditions documented as abusive (head shaving, pills discarded, forced rectal exams in some contexts). So materially below 0.35, above 0.15 slightly? Actually I think the 0.15 tier is warranted when "detainees often spend months in pretrial custody where beatings are common, courts rarely investigate, capital provision exists." Here, the criminalisation is narrower (disguise to enter women-only space — but enforced against appearance generally), penalty capped at 1 year, no capital. But the torture-level rectal exams and the unresolved multi-year detention are documented.

That is severity 4 territory.

So the combined score: high probability of outing × severity ~4 → around 0.15–0.25. I'll go 0.18.
